name: Incline Chest Press Machine
movementPattern: Horizontal and inclined chest press - guided machine
grip: Pronated or neutral grip on guided machine press handles.
description: Perform a seated press on an incline chest machine, pressing along a fixed upward arc that emphasizes the upper clavicular portion of the chest.
setup: Adjust the seat so the press handles sit level with the upper chest.
Sit firmly with back and head resting against the incline backrest, feet flat on the floor.
Grip the handles firmly with forearms aligned with the machine levers.
instructions: Press the handles forward and upward along the machine track until the arms are extended without locking the elbows.
Keep the head and upper back firmly braced against the back pad.
Pause under control at extension, then lower slowly until a comfortable chest stretch is achieved.
Do not let the weight stack touch down abruptly between repetitions.
cues: Keep back glued to the pad.
Press up along the machine angle.
commonMistakes: Lifting shoulders or upper back off the backrest at lockout.
Arching the lower back excessively to change the pressing angle.
Letting the weight plates slam at the bottom of the movement.

logging.example: Weight pin set to 55 kg: record 55 kg selected machine load.
logging.note: Machine lever arms, cams, and pulley ratios vary widely across manufacturers; record the selected stack pin or plate load without assuming 1:1 free-weight equivalency.

variantNote: Dedicated seated incline chest press machine with approx. 45-degree backrest. Levers travel along a guided incline path.
